title: Time Jump: 08:00 Friday, Muddy Boil at Station 18+50

fields.scenarioTitle: Eighteen Hours — Rising Crest, Evacuation Clock & Levee Fight
fields.narration:
EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE. It is now 08:00 CDT, Friday 23 April 2027. We have moved 34 hours past 22:00 Wednesday. CFDI4 on the Route 38 bridge piers reads 22.0 feet and is still rising, about 0.07 feet an hour. The forecast in force is still the 12:00 Wednesday issuance, which the Weather Service reaffirmed at 06:00 this morning: major flooding, with a crest near 23.4 feet at 06:00 Saturday. Cedar Hollow has been under water since Thursday afternoon. The evacuation and the Hollow Court move went the way the Coordinator's Wednesday-evening decision set them. Route 38 bottoms and Hollow Road are closed. Pump Station 1 has run on diesel since 22:04 Wednesday. Its day tank was topped up from county stock at 15:30 Thursday and now reads just above half. Levee patrols are on the 24-hour rotation, two-person teams on foot. Every crew is on its third straight day.

At 08:02 this call comes in to the Superintendent on county VHF channel 4:

"District, L-3. Emergency report. Station 18+50, Hollow Creek low spot, on the landside about 25 feet out from the toe. Sand boil, the cone's about 18 inches across. The water is MUDDY and it's boiling steady, about a pencil-thick flow. Ground's wet around it out to about 10 feet. There's a second wet spot near 18+70, clear so far. Stage at the bridge was 22.0 at 08:00. Freeboard at the low spot looks like about 2.9 feet. No cracks or slumps on the crown. We've got 60 bags in the truck. Logged 08:02, station 18+50, stage 22.0."
worldState: CFDI4 (Route 38 bridge piers): 22.0 ft at 08:00, rising about 0.07 ft an hour. That puts it near 23.4 ft early Saturday.
Forecast in force: 12:00 Wednesday issuance, reaffirmed 06:00 Friday. MAJOR flooding, crest near 23.4 ft at 06:00 Saturday, with about ±0.5 ft of uncertainty.

Cedar Hollow has been flooded since Thursday afternoon. Route 38 bottoms, Hollow Road, River Road south of Mill Street and the Mill Street underpass are all closed. Levee Road is still open to the public.

Pump Station 1 has been on diesel since 22:04 Wednesday. The day tank was topped up at 15:30 Thursday and now reads just above half. At this burn rate it runs dry around 03:30 Saturday, before the crest. The utility feeder from Substation 4 is still out, with no restore time.
Levee patrol: 24-hour rotation, two-person foot teams every 2 hours, Superintendent on site.

08:02 emergency report from Team L-3: a sand boil carrying MUDDY water at Station 18+50, Hollow Creek low spot, about 25 ft landside of the toe. A second wet spot at about 18+70 is clear so far. Freeboard at the low spot is about 2.9 ft. No cracks or slumps on the crown. L-3 has 60 bags in the truck.
The USACE Rock Island District offer of a geotechnical engineer (email, 16:41 Wednesday) is still open.
Crews are on their third straight day of shifts.
fields.facilitatorNote: The plan treats a muddy boil as an emergency report, and the stage has passed the district's 22.0 ft trigger (sand boil rings, Levee Road closed, Corps technical assistance). Read the L-3 call in a flat, urgent radio voice. Before the boil, mention the fuel only as a tank level. Let players work out that it runs dry around 03:30 Saturday.

instructorNote: Watch for these steps. LEV reports the muddy boil to the Superintendent and the Coordinator at once with the station number, rings it without sealing it, closes Levee Road and accepts the USACE engineer. EM sends WebEOC requests to Iowa HSEMD for bags, pumps and Guard crews, each with a delivery point and needed-by time, citing levee distress, and starts tracking the 18-hour evacuation clock for the 340 homes behind the levee before the stage nears the plant's flood line. Also check whether anyone catches that PS1 fuel runs out before Saturday's crest.
